findings.reason: without a clause naming the fate of `_provider_jitter` and its test, the node can land a dead function plus a green test that asserts a superseded mechanism, so the file's green is no evidence the stamp signal changed — which is the failure the done-when rubric exists to catch.
findings.text: the done-when replaces the measured-jitter threshold with half the clock's window, which leaves `_provider_jitter` (reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:864) with no production caller — its only caller is `_stamp_moved_past_jitter` (:842,825) — and leaves `tests/test_a_lift_survives_reset_jitter.py::test_the_provider_jitter_is_the_spread_of_the_stamp_history` (:188) asserting the rule the plan removed; the plan says the file "keeps its one-second and full-window cases" and brings only assertions "that a move larger than the jitter but smaller than half a window ends a lift" to the new rule, so nothing directs the orphaned function or its test to be retired, and the done-when's "no added failure against base" is satisfied precisely because that test passes identically before and after the change

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_reset_observed` (reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:802), `_stamp_moved_past_jitter` (:842), `_provider_jitter` (:864), `end_cause` + its `lift_watch` callers (reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:62,127), `published_readings` (reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:181, single-reading docstring), `WINDOW_MINUTES_CLOCK` (reckon/budget.py:3368, keys 300/10080 minutes giving the stated 2.5 h and 3.5 d halves), `tests/test_a_lift_survives_reset_jitter.py`, and §12/§14/§15 all resolve; the one extensionless h2 target resolves as `.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's done-when retires the measured-jitter threshold the stamp signal is built on but says nothing about `_provider_jitter` or its test, so a node can satisfy every bullet while leaving a function and a test that assert the rule the plan removed.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative-control log goes "under the run directory" (a durable crew run path), and the gate is the repository's own test tree, neither a session scratchpad nor a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §16 introduces no symbol and names its new test file by what it measures (`tests/test_a_reset_moves_the_window.py`); no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a code path.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a drifted `resets_at` stamp read as a rollover) is what the cited sample shows (utilisation 0.64 sits above the 0.06 grant figure, so neither utilisation signal can be the cause, leaving the stamp signal); the half-window threshold is capable of the done-when's measures; and the mechanism runs on the real code path — `_reset_observed` ← `end_cause` ← `lift_watch.sweep` (the watch stream) and ← `_in_force` ← `effective_budget`, whose pace-path caller `reckon/budget.py:2632` does supply a multi-reading history built by `_lift_history`, so the back-to-back reading the earlier review asked about has a producer.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 carries one deliverable, the stamp threshold in `_reset_observed`.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §16 declares no per-node depends-on/informs/gates (every section in this plan carries `data-links=""`, relationships live at plan level as `plan-informs=background-agent-fitness-and-dispatch-scope`), and the section it supersedes (§12, `data-status="done"`) resolves (docs/plans/a-window-paces-the-lane.html#s12).
